messages.subject: Re: reset the node color rule
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jan,

I reproduced Burak's situation in a small example.  Using the standard
demo network produced by  makeSimpleGraph, and after setting up a
nodeColor rule:

   node.types = c ('kinase', 'transcription factor', 'glycoprotein')
    colors = c ('#00FFFF', '#0088FF', '#0044FF')
    setNodeColorRule (cw, 'type', node.types, colors, mode='lookup')

I am unable to see an effect from this

    setDefaultNodeColor (cw, '#DDAAAA');     redraw (cw)

until, in the vizmapper GUI, I click on 'Node Color' and then choose
'Delete Mapping' from the popup menu.

Forgive me if I misunderstood your reply -- you mentioned  the
'delete[Node|Edge|Network]Attribute function'.  Maybe in time we could
get a function like this?

     deleteVizMap ('Node Color')

And perhaps something like this, too?

    deleteDirectVizAssignment ('Node Color', nodes=c ('A', 'B', 'C'))

In both cases, the color of nodes would fall back to the current
default.

  - Paul

Hi Paul,

the functions you mention should not be hard to implement. I'll try to
find some time to do this after my vacation (2 weeks in France).

The function I mentioned should be able to remove one attribute for all
nodes. You need to specify the name of the attribute for that. All the
'overwrite' commands create an attribute which reflects the new value of
the visual parameter. Use the getVisualBypassNames() to get a list of
what the names are of these attributes or use the attribute browser.

Cheers,

Jan

messages.subject: Re: capturing network image
messages.body_plain:
Hi Burak,

I noticed that Cytoscape's (2.8) image menu supports PDF, SVG, and
EPS. As far as I understand, these are all "vector" formats that can
be scaled up or down as much as needed. Although the "saveImage"
throws an error (I'm guessing based on CytoscapeRPC ImageIO) when
trying to use any of these from R, you can output an SVG version using
the Cytoscape menu. You could then open this SVG in Inkscape (or Adobe
Illustrator) and save a PNG at whatever resolution you like. If this
is for publication, then it shouldn't be too much trouble.

It would be nice if these formats were supported from CyRPC though.

-Robert

messages.subject: Re: getAllNodeAttributes
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

I think this problem -- which was reported by David Reiss last week -- can be solved like this:

  cw <- existing.CytoscapeWindow ('name of network goes here', copy.graph=TRUE)

getAllNode|EdgeAttributes draws data from the graphNEL (cw@graph) on the R side of things.  So by copying the Cytoscape network into an R graph, which is the effect of copy.graph=TRUE, there is attribute data for the 'getAll...' function to draw from.

Sorry the error message is not more clear.  I will fix that.

Cheers,

 - Paul

messages.subject: Re: node border line type attribute
messages.body_plain:
This appears to be

 1) a method I left out of RCytoscape -- I'll add it to the next
version
 2) a somewhat undeveloped visual mapping in Cytoscape, as you can see
if you try various values from the Visual Mapping Bypass context popup
menu.

You can make use of the few node-border-styles which work, if you
wish, using this bit of code -- which will form the heart of the

   setNodeBorderStyle

method in the next version of RCytocape:

     visual.style.name <http://visual.style.name> = 'default'
     controlling.node.attribute = 'type'
     vizmap.parameter = 'Node Line Style'
     default.line.style= 'SOLID'
     node.attribute.values = c ("kinase", "transcription factor",
"glycoprotein")
     line.styles = c ('DASH_DOT', 'EQUAL_DASH', 'DASH_DOT')

      xml.rpc (cw@uri, 'Cytoscape.discreteMapper', c...@window.id,
visual.style.name <http://visual.style.name>, controlling.node.attribute,
               vizmap.parameter, default.line.style,
node.attribute.values, line.styles)

 - Paul

messages.subject: rggobi for 3D viewing [was 3DScape]
messages.body_plain:
Mark Grimes, hoping to plot 3D distance matrices as nodes in Cytoscape, was willing to try rggobi until Cytoscape's 3D is usable.

Since rggobi is one of the perks that implicitly comes with using RCytoscape, this small email is not -completely- off topic.  But of course, feel free to ignore or delete it right away.

With a numeric matrix 'dz3' 2482 rows by 3 columns, here are instructions to load this into ggobi, assign colors by numerical range, run a '2d tour' -- the scatter plot spins in 3-space -- then brush (select) one or more points, after which you can select the corresponding data in R in the original matrix.

 library (rggobi)
  class (dz3) # [1] "matrix"
  dim (dz3)   # [1] 2482    3

 gobi = ggobi (dz3)
   # use some colors by level:  Tools->Automatic Brushing->Constant Bin Width -> Apply -> Close
   # interactively:  View->2D Tour
   # select one point (I chose the gray point that sits off by itself in 3-space):
   #    Interaction-> Brush

 print (which (selected.GGobiData (gobi [1])))                    #  2258
 print (rownames (dz3) [which (selected.GGobiData (gobi [1]))])   #  "TPM3"
 print (dz3 [which (selected.GGobiData (gobi [1])),])             #  194.8816 -1350.5168   420.7481
